$comment: Config for the PreToolUse hooks. command-guard.mjs (run_command) ships DISABLED: enable it in .agents/hooks.json by setting "frontier-guard".enabled to true; its built-in rules always apply (catastrophic commands -> deny, risky commands -> force_ask). orchestrator-guard.mjs (edit tools + invoke_subagent) ships ENABLED: it denies workspace edits and malformed invoke_subagent waves in the ORCHESTRATOR conversation only, and returns "orchestratorGuardPassthrough" for every other call. "allow" (default) auto-approves those calls, bypassing Antigravity's permission prompt: this matches users who run with always-proceed / proceed-in-sandbox. "ask" makes Antigravity prompt instead (cached 'Always allow' grants still apply). Test changes with: node --test .agents/hooks/test/hooks.test.mjs

defaultDecisionOptions.ask: Recommended. Commands that match no rule go through Antigravity's normal permission prompt, which still honours the user's cached 'Always allow' grants.
defaultDecisionOptions.allow: Auto-approves every command that matches no rule and BYPASSES the user's permission policy. Fewer prompts in a trusted sandbox, but any destructive command the rules do not cover runs without asking. Use only in disposable environments.

extraRulesFormat: Each entry is { "pattern": "<JavaScript regex, case-insensitive>", "reason": "<short label>" }. Invalid regexes are ignored. Example: { "pattern": "\\bprisma\\s+migrate\\s+reset\\b", "reason": "prisma migrate reset" }

orchestratorGuardPassthroughOptions.allow: Default. Edits by workers and valid invoke_subagent waves are auto-approved (Antigravity always-proceed / proceed-in-sandbox behaviour).
orchestratorGuardPassthroughOptions.ask: Those calls go through Antigravity's normal permission prompt instead. Use this if you review edits by hand.
